title: Arupadai Veedu
quotes: “If Muruga laughs in Thiruparankundram, the hills of Thiruthani will echo!”
“As I say your name, Muruga, my tongue and heart taste sweetness!”
intro: Lord Muruga (also known by various other beautiful names – Karthikeya, Kumara, Subramanian, Skanda, Vadivela, Arumugam) is born to Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvathi to destroy a demon called Soorapadma who was terrorizing Earth and the Heavens. He is Lord Ganesha’s younger brother. He is described as the God of Tamil, War and Mountainous Regions. He is depicted as a strong, handsome, young man who rides a peacock/rooster and carries the Vel (spear) that vanquishes enemies in battle.

There are 6 temples in Tamil Nadu, India that depict Him in various stages of his divine life where He imparts several lessons to be followed by followers, destroys demons and gains favor of Gods and humans to gain two beautiful brides and to fulfill His purpose. Here they are in chronological order as in Skanda Puranam:

items.name: Swami Malai
items.text: Lord Muruga is in the form of a little boy giving knowledge to His Father, Lord Shiva. Even though, Lord Shiva is the Almighty God of Destruction, he is depicted as a disciple (Shishya) standing with folded hands covering his mouth while seated Baby Boy Muruga teaches Him the meaning of the word Om. This episode teaches us that knowledge can be in the littlest of people and we should be ready to stoop down to learn.

items.name: Pazhani
items.text: Sibling Rivalry between Lord Ganesha and Muruga over who gets to eat a magic fruit leads to a challenge which Muruga loses due to technicalities. He throws away all his possessions and leaves the heavens as an ascetic (Aandi) to the Hills of Palani. His favorite poetess, Avvaiyar, promises Goddess Parvathi that she will return with him. Muruga who doesn’t stop for all the pleas of His parents and sibling stops to listen to the Word Garland that Avvaiyar braids. She “admonishes” Him singing that He, himself, is the divine fruit that people aspire to achieve and that He should not engage in petty quarrels with His brother. He acquiesces and follows her back to the heavens. This episode implores us to reduce anger and look deeper to find that there is always some treasure hidden beneath the surface of unfair situations. In this case, Avvaiyar’s beautiful poetry became world renowned as a results of this event. Lord Muruga grows up training in all the arts, languages and war weaponry. He becomes well known for his skills at war.

items.name: Thiruchendur
items.text: A seaside town hailed as the sacred bloody battlefield where Lord Muruga destroys Demon Soorapadman and fulfills His purpose. I interpret this as a win for good over evil. This war is staged every year in this temple.

items.name: Thiruparamkundram
items.text: Lord Muruga gains favor of Lord Indra (King of the Heavens) with His victory over Soorapadman and gains the hand of Lord Indra’s daughter, Princess Deivanai. The divine marriage takes place in this temple with all the Gods showering blessings on the young couple. The positive vibes and happiness in this temple are palpable.

items.name: Thiruthani
items.text: Valli, the daughter of a tribal chieftain, is a fervent devotee of Lord Muruga and wants to be united with Him. He tests her devotion and then accepts her. This divine marriage takes place in Vallimalai (The Mountain of Valli) and they settle in the town of Thiruthani.

items.name: Pazhamudhircholai
items.text: After a short quarrel, He sets up home amicably with Goddesses Deivanai and Valli in Pazhamudhircholai. Even the Gods have jealousy! The name of this town translates as “The Garden where fruits fall”. There is another story about Poetess Avvaiyar associated with this town. Lord Muruga (forever, the mischievous one) revels in testing the intelligence and devotion of His followers. He takes the form of a young boy and climbs up a tree in this orchard on a hot day. Avvaiyar rests under this tree and is famished. The boy asks her what type of fruit she wants – Roasted or Raw. She doesn’t understand and says Raw just to appease the boy. He shakes the tree and some fruits fall. She blows the sand off the fruits to eat them when the boy reminds her that they are Raw not Roasted and she need not blow on them to cool them. She realizes that this is not an ordinary boy. Lord Muruga reveals Himself to her and blesses her. This episode teaches us again that knowledge can be in the most unexpected place and keeping our mind’s eye open is the only way to absorb it.
